reason: At base the object JIT fastpass keeps the value written alongside a swallowed issue, so safeParse({}) returns data with key a present, contradicting the expectation of no key.

The PR guards both the issue concat and the value assignment on presence, so after the fix an absent optional key with a failing check yields success and no key in the output, and a present failing value fails.
At base the paragraph continuation lookahead only treats spaces-only lines as blank, so a tab-only line is absorbed as a lazy continuation and the two lines merge into one paragraph.
The PR widens the blank-line lookahead to [ \t]+ so a tab-only line now interrupts the paragraph, producing two paragraphs after the fix.
The PR only touches the error stack-decoration path in the request catch handler; successful JSON response parsing is unrelated and works by default at base.
The stack-decoration fix does not affect response parsing; a 200 application/json response is still parsed into an object by default.
The PR only widens the negative-number regex; ordinary boolean flag parsing like --verbose is unaffected and works at base.
The negative-number regex change is unrelated to boolean flag parsing, so --verbose is still recognized after the fix.
At base JsonTreeReader.nextInt has no ASCII validation and Integer.parseInt coerces full-width Unicode digits to 123, so no error is raised as the test expects.
The PR adds validateAscii to JsonTreeReader.nextInt/nextLong for string tokens, so the tree-based conversion of full-width digits throws a MalformedJsonException after the fix.
At base the search_path regex only matches [a-zA-Z0-9$] runs, so test-db is split into two schema names test and db, contrary to the expected single schema.
The PR replaces the allowlist regex with a delimiter blocklist, so test-db is kept as one schema name and the SQL is set search_path to "test-db".

The PR only fixes buffer recycling in ByteBufferUtil.fromStream; it does not touch the request/transformation pipeline, and Glide applies configured transformations by default unless dontTransform is set.
The buffer-leak fix is unrelated to transformation eligibility; a request with center-crop and no dontTransform still gets transformed after the change.
At base the computed allowedSymbolsAndAlphanumerics already unions the configured allowed symbols with alphanumerics, so an identifier using the allowed symbol passes the naming rule.
The PR is a behavior-preserving caching refactor: the cached set is refreshed whenever allowedSymbols changes, so the allowed symbol still passes after the change.
The PR only adds a missing <cstdint> include in CharData.h for GCC 15; it does not affect Image src data-URI handling, and node-canvas decodes percent-encoded SVG data URIs before parsing.

The Afrikaans-locale PR is unrelated to shift semantics; arrow shift(hours=10) uses relativedelta wall-clock addition on an aware datetime, yielding 2025-03-09T04:30-05:00, not the expected 05:30-05:00 accounting for the skipped hour.
The cstdint include fix is unrelated to image loading, so behavior is unchanged: a percent-encoded SVG data URI still loads and can be drawn.
The PR only changes Cookie header directive parsing; form-urlencoded content decoding is unaffected, and an empty body decodes fine into a type whose fields are all optional.
The cookie-header parsing change is unrelated to form-urlencoded content decoding; an empty body still decodes into an all-optional type at head.
The PR only fixes spelling in a test file and a comment; afero MemMapFs.Remove already rejects removing a non-empty directory, leaving the directory and its file intact.
Spelling fixes do not change filesystem behavior; Remove on a non-empty in-memory directory still returns an error and preserves contents.
The PR is a test-only JSON flags fix unrelated to the schema Comparator; DBAL rename detection handles ambiguous candidates without an undefined-key warning at this revision.
Same unrelated test-only JsonTest change at head; the Comparator rename detection behavior is unchanged, so the comparison still completes without an undefined-key warning.
The Afrikaans locale PR is unrelated; arrow shift(hours=10) performs wall-clock relativedelta addition, yielding 04:30-05:00 rather than the expected 05:30-05:00 that accounts for the skipped hour.
The PR only touches the circuitbreaker module predicate handling; the ratelimiter module is untouched and its semaphore refresh guard keeps replenishing after the limit is lowered.
Same unrelated circuit-breaker change at head; the rate limiter refresh task continues running and keeps admitting calls at the new limit.
The PR changes prefer-template, not no-var; ESLint no-var declines to autofix a var captured by an earlier-called function (TDZ hazard), so the script keeps var semantics and prints undefined.
The prefer-template ASI fix is unrelated to no-var; the indirectly-invoked-before-declaration case is not autofixed, so execution still prints undefined at head.
The PR only fixes logformatter_adapter message adaptation; JOBDIR persistence (disk request queue, seen requests) is unaffected, so a restarted SitemapSpider resumes remaining URLs.
Same unrelated logging change at head; the persisted scheduler queue is replayed on restart, so the spider crawls remaining pages before closing.

The PR only changes the --sanitize preprocessor; the highlight-line background fill at terminal-width 1 with a double-width char is a separate width-underflow path that the sanitize change does not affect, and the changelog suggests this class of capacity-overflow was only fixed for the snip separator.

The sanitize regex/trigger change is unrelated to row-background rendering; the theme background fill across a 1-column terminal with double-width chars still hits the same width-underflow panic at head.
The PR only optimizes the syslog parser regex; out_file buffer/symlink handling is untouched, and per-chunk-key symlink expansion creates a symlink for each key in a mixed batch.
Same unrelated syslog-parser change at head; out_file still expands the symlink placeholder per chunk, updating the symlink for the follow-up key.
The PR changes ConcurrentBag handoff parking only; pool-name generation uses an internal counter and does not synchronize on the system properties object, so construction is unaffected at base.
Same unrelated ConcurrentBag change at head; pool-name generation does not lock the shared system-properties object, so concurrent pool creation completes.
The PR only fixes SORT ACL key extraction; BGSAVE/RDB persistence is untouched and a few-MB dataset saves fine on a 32-bit standalone server.
Same unrelated db.c ACL parser change at head; automatic background saving at the configured save point still completes successfully on 32-bit.
The PR changes cwd context bookkeeping only; Neovim CTRL-A/CTRL-X use a string-based path for numbers too large for 64-bit, so the 50-digit increment preserves all digits at base.
Same unrelated cwd fix at head; the large-number string arithmetic path for CTRL-X still decrements the 50-digit number digit-for-digit.
The PR changes external file cache block reclamation only; || with a list and an untyped NULL binds to list_concat with the NULL cast to the list type, yielding INTEGER[] NULL at base.
Same unrelated file-cache change at head; || and list_concat both bind the NULL literal to INTEGER[], so the two typeof results match.
The PR changes ScrollBar drag input handling only; RefCounted PREDELETE delivery to a live script instance is standard engine behavior and unaffected at base.
Same unrelated ScrollBar change at head; dropping the last reference still delivers NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE while the object is valid, printing the assigned member.
The PR is about tree categorical splitting; f_regression with force_finite (default) assigns F=0.0 and p=1.0 to constant columns while suppressing warnings via errstate, unchanged at base.
Same unrelated tree change at head; r_regression suppresses sqrt warnings via np.errstate and clips correlations into [-1,1] with force_finite.
The PR is a UI-only swagger-ui change; Vault agent file sink mode handling is untouched and applies the configured octal mode at base.
Same unrelated UI change at head; the file sink still applies mode 0600 to the token file.
At base write_usage with empty args discards the prefix via wrap_text("") returning an empty string, so the first line is blank rather than "Usage: cli" for a command whose usage pieces render empty.
The fix emits the prefix line directly when args is empty, so the first help line is exactly "Usage: cli" after the PR.
The PR only fixes IPv6 host/port parsing in the dev server and test client; Flask still serializes a returned dict as compact application/json.
Same unrelated IPv6 parsing fix at head; dict-returning views still produce application/json with compact separators.
The PR only changes DEPRECATED_ALIASES lookup for unhashable generic aliases; required-field validation is core pydantic behavior that raises a missing-field error at base.
Same unrelated schema-generation fix at head; omitting a required field still raises a validation error identifying the field as missing.
WARN and WARNING are the same constant; with echo off the sqlalchemy logger sits at WARNING so no INFO SQL records are captured, and echo on logs statements, unchanged at base.
The WARN->WARNING rename is behavior-neutral; echo-off suppression and echo-on logging are identical at head.

Aliased select columns get generated attribute methods just like real columns, so steady-state reads are direct method calls with comparable cost; the method_missing thread-safety fix does not affect this at base.
After the thread-safety fix, generated attribute methods are still used for steady-state reads; the one-time method_missing path is amortized, keeping the ratio under 20x.
At base, called listeners accumulate in the callStack per dispatch, so dispatching twice with one listener yields two getCalledListeners entries.
The PR deduplicates called listeners into calledListenerInfos (one entry per listener per event), so two dispatches with the same single listener produce one entry, not the two the test expects.

The PR only rewrites COMPREPLY assignment as append loops and fixes pushd error handling; per-subcommand scoping is determined by the __complete callback arguments, which are unchanged, so each hook still returns subcommand-scoped values at base.

COMPREPLY is initialized fresh by bash per completion attempt and the modified branches are mutually exclusive per invocation, so the append form preserves behavior; subcommand scoping via __complete is untouched.
At base (qs 6.13.0), repeated bare query keys are merged into an array without applying arrayLimit, so 25 repeated ids keys parse as an ordered array of 25 strings.
qs 6.14.0 applies arrayLimit (default 20) to repeated bare keys too, so 25 repeated ids keys parse into a plain object with numeric indices, not an array.
At base get_environ_proxies takes only the url argument, so calling it with just a URL works and returns the environment proxy dict.
The PR adds a required no_proxy parameter to get_environ_proxies and should_bypass_proxies, so calling get_environ_proxies with only a URL raises TypeError at head.

At base, parse_unit_value rejects tokens not starting with a digit or '-', so '.foons' returns None there and falls through to normal bare-word string parsing, yielding the string '.foons' with no parse error.
At head '.foons' enters parse_unit_value, but its unit suffix 'foons' matches no known duration/filesize unit, so the function returns None and the token still parses as a plain string.

At base, the cURL handler connects a sink/write callback even for HEAD requests; with an Accept-Encoding header this produces the broken behavior the PR removes (the PR exists precisely because HEAD-with-sink failed), so the request does not complete cleanly.
At head, no sink or write function is connected for HEAD requests, so the HEAD request with Accept-Encoding completes and returns a valid response without fatal error.

At base, maps inside assertion diffs fall back to inspect and the improper list inside the map breaks clean diff formatting (the issue this PR solves), so the failure output is not the clean match-failure diff expected.
At head, maps are converted to AST representation for diffing so the match failure on %{bar: [1 | 2]} is formatted as a normal assertion failure without an extra formatting crash.

At base, css_props registered a teardown that removes the wrapper element on re-render, so after toggling the dynamic component the inner component loses its scoped custom property (color is no longer red).
At head, the element-removal teardown is gone and dynamic components with css props hydrate correctly, so the inner text stays red before and after the toggle with no hydration error.
At base, the plugin matched any code containing 'new URL' and 'import.meta.url' and its regex used \s* between tokens, so a multi-line new URL(...) reference was still detected and the asset emitted.

At head, the new hook filter /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/ has no dotAll flag, so '.' cannot cross the newlines of a multi-line new URL(...) call; the transform is skipped and the asset is never emitted.
At base, fzf does not export the current item to the preview environment, so a NUL-delimited item causes no problem and the preview command runs and shows 'ok'.

At head, FZF_CURRENT_ITEM is exported with the raw item text; an item containing NUL bytes puts NUL into an environment string, which makes spawning the child preview process fail instead of running 'echo ok'.
At base, edge-to-edge relied on deprecated layout flags and switching back from immersiveSticky did not reliably restore the system bars (the issue this PR fixes), so the bars stay hidden.

At head, PlatformPlugin uses EdgeToEdge.enable/WindowCompat and restores proper inset behavior on mode switches, so entering edgeToEdge after immersiveSticky shows the status and navigation bars again.
At base, ruff has no multiple-assignment-in-case-pattern check at all, so 'case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes):' reports no syntax error even in preview mode.

At head, the new visitor inserts both the class-pattern keyword attr and the bound variable into the same name set, so 'case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes):' is falsely reported as a duplicate assignment under --preview.
At base, decoding two blocks into a value-slice field pre-populated with one entry indexes past the slice length and panics with slice index out of range, so decoding does not finish cleanly.
At head, the decoder grows the destination slice with reflect.Append when the index exceeds its length, so both blocks decode into exactly two entries and the placeholder is overwritten.
At base, a mocked now keeps the timezone the mock moment carried (America/Los_Angeles) when no timezone is pinned, so now() formats as the LA time rather than the UTC default.
At head, the mocked instance is converted to date_default_timezone_get() (UTC) when no timezone is given, so Carbon::now() matches the reference moment's UTC representation.
At base, /^[/\\]{2}[^/\\]+/ matches none of '///test.com', '/<TAB>//test.com', or '/\\/test.com', so they are not classified as protocol-relative, contrary to the expected result.

At head, the expanded regex /^([/\\]\s*){2,}[^/\\]/ accepts three or more slashes, whitespace between slashes, and mixed slash/backslash starts, so all three strings classify as protocol-relative with no explicit protocol.
The PR only swaps asBytes() for getBytesInternal() inside combineOrdered/combineUnordered; MD5 hashing of "abc" is untouched and already produces the standard digest at base.
The change is a behavior-preserving micro-optimization of hash combining; MD5('abc') still yields 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72 at head.
At base the generator already produces a working client for an interface with a valid GET-style attribute; moving diagnostic descriptors to a dedicated class does not affect generation.
The PR is a pure refactor of diagnostic descriptor locations with unchanged codes and behavior, so source generation and the issued GET request work the same at head.
At base the HTTP/1 client reads a plain 200 OK body fine; the PR only removes redundant 'continue' statements and does not change control flow.
Removing last-in-loop 'continue' statements is behavior-neutral (clippy's needless_continue only fires on redundant ones), so the plain HTTP/1.1 GET body read works identically at head.

At base, to_iso8601(date, :basic) on a non-ISO-calendar date converts to Calendar.ISO but then calls to_iso8601() without the format, silently returning the extended '2001-01-01' instead of '20010101'.
At head, the requested format is passed through after the calendar conversion, so the Holocene date formats as '2001-01-01' by default and '20010101' with :basic.
At base on PHP 8.2+, setEndDate() updates the internal end date but the native DatePeriod 'end' property keeps the original 2024-09-30 value, so the two reads disagree with the expectation.
At head, syncNativePeriod() re-initializes the parent DatePeriod after setEndDate(), so both ->end and getEndDate() report 2025-06-15.
At base there is no whitespace validation of the request URI, so a path containing a newline is transmitted in the request line without any error being raised.
At head, headline raises HTTP::RequestError 'Invalid request URI' when the path matches /\s/, so the client refuses to send the newline-containing request before transmission.
The PR only changes Albanian (sq) locale data; the default English conversion of 1,000,000 to 'one million' and 2,000,000 to 'two million' already works at base.
English number-to-words output is unaffected by the Albanian plural fix, so both conversions still return 'one million' and 'two million' at head.
The PR only changes JVM property loading for non-String Properties entries; singleton resolution with no custom properties is unrelated and already returns the identical instance twice at base.
Filtering non-string property keys does not touch DI resolution, so the singleton component still resolves to the same instance on both lookups at head.

At base, replaceElement already appends the new pair, swaps it into position, and removes the old one, preserving order, and the duplicate-key precondition already raises; the PR is a behavior-preserving refactor.
At head the same replace logic runs through the shared OrderedSet primitive with the value overwritten in place, so order and the duplicate-key precondition behave identically.
At base, parseSizeInBytes already clamps negative parsed sizes to 0 via the manual if-check, so '-5MB' returns 0 bytes.
At head, max(cast.ToInt(sizeStr), 0) is exactly equivalent to the previous manual clamp, so '-5MB' still returns 0.

At base, findCaseInsensitivePathRec uses children[0] for a wildChild node; with a static child first, the switch hits the default case and panics 'invalid node type' for both the mis-cased static path and the unmatched path, so there is no clean redirect or ordinary 404.

At head, static children are tried via indices before falling back to the wildcard child at the end of the array, so /PREFIX/XXX redirects to /prefix/xxx and /prefix/a/b/c yields a normal not-found without panic.
At base, Numeric.Int64Value on Numeric{Valid: true} reaches toBigInt which returns the nil Int when Exp is 0, and IsInt64 then dereferences nil and panics instead of returning zero.
At head, toBigInt returns big.NewInt(0) when Int is nil, so both Float64Value and Int64Value on the valid-but-empty Numeric report zero with no panic.
The PR only changes renderer tab-stop handling, unrelated to the run loop's shutdown path; calling Quit from another goroutine already makes Run return promptly at base.
Tab-stop rendering changes do not affect program shutdown, so Quit from outside the update loop still ends the run call without hanging at head.

At base, run_until_cancelled builds and polls the wrapped future even when the token is already cancelled (cancellation was not checked first), so the panicking operation starts and the expected clean cancelled outcome does not occur.
At head, an already-cancelled token makes run_until_cancelled return None immediately without ever polling the wrapped future, so no panic is raised and the operation resolves as cancelled.
The PR only skips loading unreachable ignore files in the directory walker; case-insensitive pattern matching is unaffected and already reports all case variants at base.
Skipping ignore-file loading for unreachable directories does not change match semantics, so case-insensitive search still finds every matching line at head.
At base, a skip_deserializing field with no explicit default already gets Default::default() via the nested if, so the omitted field deserializes to its type's default (e.g. 0).
The PR just collapses the nested if into a single equivalent condition (container_default.is_none() && skip_deserializing), so the skipped field still receives its type's default at head.
